Our best performances came from Charles Gillett, who really fought in the 400 metres hurdles and Adrian Major, 4th in his fastest mile so far this season.
Our best performances on the track came from Charles Gillett in the 220 , Dave Rees in the 440 and Adrian Major in the mile, while Mark McNair ran a very promising first three miles.

110m H: An unexpectedly good run from Bob Couillault just back from holiday. 400m H: But for hitting the last hurdle, Charles Gillett must have beaten his best. Again the finish was close and standard high.

Ford broke his own Club 400m hurdles record (55.4) when he ran 55.3 at Portsmouth on July 16th, in finishing second for the Army in the inter-services championships. He has since lost his record to Charles Gillett, who has clocked 54.5.

Charles Gillett was another to be eliminated in his heat, but his performances over the intermediate hurdles this year suggests he has the ability to reach a future final in this, Britain's strongest event.
Steve Inman (Pole Vault) also posted to Ireland. Charlie Gillett (400m Hurdles, 4 X 440 Relay) Injured. John Mitchell (Long Jump, Sprints) Injured.
Our second ranking man, Charlie Gillett, is also a class hurdler. We have a very promising youth coming through in Martin Bloice, who has already done times that would do most seniors credit.

Nevertheless, it only requires a modest improvement for this man to shoot up to the very top. The 400m. hurdles sees Mel Ford in 16th place, and Charlie Gillett in 43rd. Swiss member Henry Pfenninger is 12th in the pole vault.
He will have fine backing from LEE SULLIVAN, MICK MARSHALL, CLIFF BROOKS and CHARLIE GILLETT. 400m One of the weak spots, although I hope I'am proved wrong.
Steve also won the long jump and contributed to our 4 x 100m winning squad. Our other winners of the meeting were Charlie Gillett in the 400m hurdles and Arnold Bentt in the triple jump.
However, I would like to welcome back after periods of absence Jim Vivian and Charlie Gillett both of whom turned out regularly thereby adding strength to the team.
Steve White and Jim Vivian, who we were very pleased to see back on the track this year, both completed sprint doubles and Charlie Gillett won both the 400m hurdles and the 400m 'B' race.
Charlie Gillett won the 400 hurdles with a great run, lopping 2 seconds off of his seasonal best and he also managed to pip a tiring Snowy Brooks on the tape in the flat event.

Our Track Secretary Philip Gee ran a powerful 400m to win the 'B' race and Charlie Gillett gave of his best with a 400 Hurdles 'B' win, a 3rd in the 'A' 200m where he was only just caught on the line with the first four clocking the same time, and his usual sparkling run round the third leg bend in the short relay.
Track Vice-Captain Charlie Gillett improved on his best times for 1973 in the 400m flat and hurdle races and looks as if he could go faster still.
Hopkins gave a glimpse of his all round ability with a first ever 400m hurdles run of 58.6 whilst Charlie Gillett, who has yet to lose a Southern League one lap event this year, took the 'A' race.

Charlie Gillett finished a metre or so down in this but turned the tables when it came to the two longer sprints. An 800 metre/ 1500 metre double was scored by John Stow who was untroubled over either distance.

After a bright start our lack of depth began to tell and despite great efforts from many people, especially Snowy Brooks, Charlie Gillett, Steve White and Arnold Bentt, we gradually slipped behind Mitcham and it looked as though we would have to settle for second place.

Superb baton changing from Mick to Charlie Gillett and on to Steve gave us a comfortable win in the 4 x 100m and now, as so often in these meetings, the overall result depended on the 4 x 400m.

Mick Marshall narrowly beat Charlie Gillett in a tight 200m, having gained 3rd in the 100m and Philip Gee was at his most aggressive, tearing out that first 200m in the one lap event and hanging on to gain a medal.

But with only two other winners, Charlie Gillett and Mick Marshall, we were not good enough to hold the Essex Club. We can only pride ourselves on seeing how obviously pleased these clubs are when they do manage to defeat Belgrave.
SPOTLIGHT ON CHARLIE GILLETT continued from page 21 on "chat-shows" on TV, for whenever there is anything to be said about contemporary music, Charlie Gillett is the man to say it.

He held Charlie Gillett off by a tenth with young Reg. breaking new ground with an 11.6 for third. Charlie later stamped his authority on the 200 and 400 metre fields with a couple of good times considering the dusty condition of the track.

Unfortunately space does not permit me to list them all but Steve White (who travels from Oxford to compete for the club) and Charlie Gillett deserve a mention for their efforts; neither ever seems to have a bad run.

Charlie Gillett enjoyed his elevation to 'A' string status, equalling his best 100 metre time and winning the 200 metres. This gave Steve White the chance to have a rest from the short events and tackle the one lap race for a change.
Charlie Gillett and Philip Gee covered the shorter sprints quite successfully and Paul Williamson made his league debut in the 'B' 400 metres with a good 2nd place.

Five times Charlie Gillett stepped onto the track to race and his record at the end of the day was remarkable. He won both his sprint heats in good times, improved on them again in the finals and then helped our relay team on it's way to 2nd place.

GERRY NORTH was selected to play in the International Athletes soccer side in a match against Radio London and Radio Medway. Playing for the radio team was none other than CHARLIE GILLETT and we understand he had a pretty good game too.
Charlie Gillett, Martin Scott and Cliff Brooks covered for us in the sprints the latter notching up no less than seven individual performances plus a relay.
A win by Charlie Gillett over 400m gave the announcer the chance to give him some extra publicity, exhorting all to tune in to Charlie's "Honky Tonk" on Radio London.
Charlie Gillett chipped in with an emergency 400m as Martin Scott took on Steve's mantle in the 200m and both were on or near their seasonal bests.

Highlights included 22.9 for Charlie Gillett and 23.1 for Jim Evans over 200m, 49.8/400 Steve White, sub-50 from Steve and Charlie in the 4x400, 14:35.0/5000 from John Stow, 13.21/TJ from Steve Crosbie, 3.35/PV from Reg Hopkins ................................

Top honours on this scorching day went to Charlie Gillett who ran inside 50 seconds for the first time in many years. It was an all out effort all the way from the outside lane and it wasn't until coming off the final bend that Chas. caught sight of one of his rivals for the first time in the race.
Most spectators would have backed Charlie Gillett in the 200m, however, where Jim got off to a marvellous start and, drawn in a lane outside Charlie, actually drew away for another clear victory.
Charlie Gillett always gives all he's got and it must have surprised many to see this 22.9/200 metre man breathing down Comrades Marathoner Arthur Bruce's neck.

CHARLIE GILLETT, one of our leading track men, continues to grow more popular on Radio London.
